kind: Independent classification challenge; read-only source investigation, not an activity plan or acceptance

conclusion.decision: Keep fs/terminal capabilities undeclared for the currently reviewed route. The six source controls establish unsolicited write requests and unhandled callback rejection, not sole-write dependency. Do not count the two implementations accepted or call all remaining investigation external-only.

sourceFacts.claim: Both complete permission handlers call writeProposedEdit after edit approval, then reply once/always. writeProposedEdit invokes writeTextFile with void; the outer catch does not await its promise. Separate diffContentForPatch handles display.

The six existing controlled cases have mocked filesystem/diff/connection ports. Both rejection cases record writeCallback, then permissionReply once, then unhandled rejection. They neither execute the real edit tool nor establish process/file outcome. callback_absent is not an actual AgentSideConnection absence proof.
OpenCode exact tagged edit tool requests permission, then itself writes through FSUtil, followed by formatting and file events. Client callback is therefore not the only source-visible writer.
Kilo exact tagged edit tool requests permission, then itself calls EncodedIO.write with original encoding, followed by formatting and sync.
Kilo EncodedIO encodes text and executes own filesystem operations through its sandbox-aware path.
Official ACP requires checking client fs capability before calling; absence/false disallows the call. write_text_file is an actual write/create operation and empty result means success.

Local official schema write request carries sessionId, absolute path, content and opaque meta. It has no standardized toolCallId, prior-approval token, encoding, expected file version or hash. Their absence does not make implementation impossible, but prevents pretending those facts were supplied.

Current Farfold initialize does not advertise file execution capabilities and pump returns official method_not_found for unsupported requests. This remains honest failure, not an implementation or verified compatibility claim.

inferencesNotRuntimeProof: The callback may serve client/editor synchronization, consistent with ACP documentation, but neither exact handler documents that intent; do not label it merely a preview.
A blind additional writer can compete with the Agent-owned write/format and may not preserve the Agent-owned encoding/sandbox semantics. No actual lost bytes or sandbox bypass was reproduced here.
Implementing a successful client writer would not fix the void-promise rejection path for denial, cancellation or IO errors; no-op success would be false evidence.
preciseRemainingFacts: Actual selected official program behavior when a current capabilities-false client rejects this request: process lifetime, permission response delivery, final tool status, actual file bytes/version and error feedback. Existing probe intercepts unhandledRejection and cannot decide CLI lifecycle.

Version-matched official behavior or supported route that capability-gates the request or safely consumes rejection. Do not patch/fork the upstream Agent or change its configuration to manufacture success.

If client fs is chosen for a demonstrated required route: explicit Farfold-owned permission scope and lifetime, exact connection/session ownership, treatment of cancellation with work still in flight, and current-file conflict/encoding semantics. Prior native approval cannot be guessed from opaque metadata alone.

Six insufficient-material agents still need the exact official callback contract or inspectable selection path listed in requirements-followup. Missing source research is not automatically a missing account or a proven external-only blocker.
Basic prompt examples for Cursor/Copilot and partial Grok/Mistral/Qoder evidence remain narrower than all tool workflows.
implementableBoundary: A genuine necessary callback can be implemented through official typed request dispatch, exact session owner validation, real scoped approval and real completion/error responses; that is not a second Agent loop. Generic terminal execution is not justified by these write-only cases.
Keep existing honest unsupported responses and permission/tool events; do not acknowledge empty success, synthesize tool completion, auto-retry, or ignore callback errors to force acceptance.

ARCH-44 and shared condition at requirements line 53 permit necessary compliant callbacks. PRODUCT section 11 line 185 describes the file-delivery path and does not by itself prove a universal callback prohibition; it also does not authorize an unrestricted host writer. Original product/data boundaries remain unchanged.
